newsitem.title: INDIA: India hopes talks with Pakistan will boost ties.
newsitem.headline: India hopes talks with Pakistan will boost ties.

text.p: Indian President Shankar Dayal Sharma was quoted as saying on Friday that foreign secretary level talks with Pakistan next week would help both countries improve bilateral relations.

"We earnestly hope that the opportunity provided by the resumption of talks will be seized to move our bilateral relations forward," the United New of India (UNI) quoted Sharma as telling Pakistan's new High Commissioner (ambassador) to India Ashraf Jehangir Qazi.
Talks between the two countries' top diplomats, stalled since January 1994, are scheduled to begin in New Delhi on March 28.
Sharma said India's approach towards the talks would be positive and constructive. "It is important at this time to look to the future and not remain mired in the past."

He said mutual cooperation between the two countries in the areas of trade, agriculture, industry, science and technology, art and culture and communications would significantly help improve relations.
India and Pakistan both won freedom from British rule 50 years ago. The two countries have fought three wars since 1947, two of them over the disputed territory of Kashmir.
